mappings.note: The consequences of filling in ponds -- dry taps and drowned settlements, both stated in the lesson. Rejected LO-37: recall, not the learner's own reasoning.
Why water is called costlier than money -- the writer's proposition. Rejected LO-41: an argued claim, not a located fact.
How groundwater is replenished and what it is for -- the lesson's own account of seepage and year-round supply. Rejected LO-37: nothing is added beyond the text.
Which 'big mistake' the lesson names. Rejected LO-38: the charge is stated, not weighed.
The two chief water problems the writer names (famine, flood). Rejected LO-40: a located pair, not the text's usefulness.
WHY the writer calls the earth a piggy bank -- grasping the ground of his comparison. Rejected LO-41, which fits the bare 'what did he compare it to' item.

What groundwater is and why it matters -- the key reasons out to farming, domestic and industrial use, none of which the lesson lists, so it draws on the learner's grasp of the real resource. Rejected LO-44: more than a gloss is wanted.
Why people began filling ponds -- greed for land, as stated. Rejected LO-37: reported.
The sense of 'two sides of one coin' -- the writer's claim about water imbalance. Rejected LO-44: the key argues the idea, it does not gloss the phrase.
Why water sources must be protected -- the key builds a case about environment and year-round supply that goes past the lesson. Rejected LO-41: no located point answers it.
Why water came to be sold -- the key cites population growth, pollution and over-extraction, none in the lesson, so the learner reasons about the real situation. Rejected LO-41 for that reason.
What follows from disregarding the water cycle -- the key brings in deforestation and concrete cover, beyond the text. Rejected LO-41: not recoverable from the lesson.
The big mistake and its bad result -- both set out in the lesson. Rejected LO-37: no independent reasoning.
What the water cycle is and where water goes -- the lesson's account. Rejected LO-44: a process, not vocabulary.
What the lesson teaches us -- its usefulness read off the whole. Rejected LO-41: no single point states it.
The hidden treasure and how it grows -- the lesson describes the seepage. Rejected LO-37: recall of the text's explanation.
Problems from misusing the water cycle -- the key reasons out falling water tables, flood and famine as a consequence chain. Rejected LO-41: the lesson does not lay this chain out.
How the WRITER explains excess and shortage -- the coin figure and the examples he chose. Rejected LO-41: the item asks about his handling of the idea, not for a fact.
How the water problem can be averted -- the key adds wells and baawdis, traditional sources the lesson does not name. Rejected LO-41 for that reason.
Purport of 'sab kuchh tham jaata hai, sab kuchh bah jaata hai' -- the key turns on the two verbs' figurative force. Rejected LO-38: a phrase, not a proposition.
'What could neglect of the water cycle lead to? Express your view' -- the learner's own reasoned response on a natural issue. Rejected LO-38: the demand is a stance, not agreement with the writer.
How we came to know where water comes from and goes -- keyed 'by reading', a point supplied by the extract itself. Rejected LO-34: the learner is not framing a question but reporting the source.
Where the river's water finally joins -- read off the extract and its picture. Rejected LO-35: the item asks a fact, not for the learner to render the scene.
Where knowledge of the water cycle comes from (the geography book) -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-40: a detail, not the text's use.

Why the passage opens with a question -- the key says it is to turn our attention on the subject and prompt reflection, which is precisely questioning in the service of better understanding. Rejected LO-41: nothing in the extract states the reason.
What we have not thought about until now -- the extract says it. Rejected LO-34: the learner reports the gap rather than framing a question.
What the earth is compared to, from the extract. Rejected LO-38, which I keep for the items asking why.
In which season nature pours water into the earth's piggy bank. Rejected LO-38: located detail.
How rainwater reaches the groundwater store (seeping and filtering). Rejected LO-37: the mechanism is in the extract.
WHY the earth is called a very large piggy bank -- the ground of the writer's comparison. Rejected LO-41, used for the bare 'what' version.
Why rainwater is called many times costlier than money -- the writer's proposition, contrasted in the key with money as mere exchange. Rejected LO-41: argued, not located.
Which sound the dry tap makes -- recall of a detail from the extract. Rejected LO-44, which I used for the blank where the sound word itself had to be supplied.
When the water comes -- located detail. Rejected LO-44: no word is glossed.
What untimely water causes (broken sleep) -- stated in the extract. Rejected LO-37: reported.
Which situation the 'soon-soon' line makes clear -- reading what the writer conveys by it. Rejected LO-41: the line does not state the conclusion.
What the writer means by 'bevakt' and the trouble it causes -- the item hinges on glossing that word. Rejected LO-41: the gloss is the demand, the consequence follows from it.
The name of the lesson the extract comes from -- placing the text. Rejected LO-41: bibliographic, not inside the passage.
The writer's name (Anupam Mishra) -- bibliographic placement. Rejected LO-41 on the same ground.
When water is everywhere (the rains). Rejected LO-37: located detail.
When water flows all around and its effect on schools -- both in the extract. Rejected LO-37: reported.
The difficulties of going out in the rains -- roads and rail lines under water, as the extract has it. Rejected LO-46: the answer is the text's, not the learner's own experience.
Why people fit motors -- to pull water, as stated. Rejected LO-37: reported.
What pulling water with a motor does -- the extract names the effect. Rejected LO-37: no reasoning added.
The summer situation in parts of the country (famine-like). Rejected LO-37: located detail.
The motor's effect on the neighbourhood -- shortage and quarrels, both in the extract. Rejected LO-37: reported.
The state of water in towns -- sold, and worse in summer, as the extract says. Rejected LO-37: no independent reasoning.
What the earth is compared to, from this extract. Rejected LO-38, kept for the 'why' item.
Where pond water reaches (the groundwater store). Rejected LO-37: stated.
Why ponds were filled in -- greed for land. Rejected LO-37: reported.
WHY the earth is likened to a clay piggy bank -- the ground of the comparison. Rejected LO-41, used for the 'what' version.
The effect of filling the ponds -- no seepage, falling water table, scarcity, all in the lesson's line of argument. Rejected LO-37: it stays inside the text.
The chief problem of the rainy season (flood). Rejected LO-37: located detail.
Which places floods affect (villages and cities alike). Rejected LO-37: stated in the extract.
The state of things when a flood comes ('everything halts'). Rejected LO-44, which I used for the item that asks the purport of that phrase.
Where water collects in the rains -- a list of places. Rejected LO-37: no reasoning asked.
The effect of a flood on daily life -- drowned homes, halted traffic, losses. Rejected LO-37: the extract supplies these.
